items.text: The vrooli-events UI is already substantially scaffolded: 12 pages (~1,949 LoC), 8+ shared components, a typed API client (`lib/api.ts`, 242 LoC) covering events/policies/violations/subscriptions/SSE, react-query polling, HashRouter wiring, sidebar Layout with health badge, and Tailwind theming via CSS variables. This item is gap-fill / completion, not greenfield.

Requirement-status drift: `scenarios/vrooli-events/requirements/05-ui-dashboard/module.json` marks REQ-UI-001..006 as `status: "complete"`, but REQ-UI-002 ("time-series chart") and REQ-UI-003 ("bar chart") have no rendered chart in the codebase — AnalyticsPage shows stat cards only, ScenarioMetricsPage shows a sortable table only. The validation refs are infrastructure tests (`utils.test.ts`, `errors.test.ts`, `selectors.test.ts`) that don't enforce chart rendering. Plan Phase 6 reconciles this.

items.topic: Scope strategy given the existing scaffold
items.context: The UI is already 12 pages and ~1,949 LoC of mostly-functional code. Most pages have working react-query / SSE wiring. The description implies we need to add charts, make settings editable, and ensure the compliance/circuit-breaker/subscription pages work. Greenfield rebuild would discard a lot of working code. Auditing and completing avoids wasted effort but requires us to trust the existing surface.

options.label: Audit existing UI and close concrete gaps (charts, editable settings, missing tests, requirement-status reconciliation)
options.rationale: Existing scaffold is well-architected and largely functional; rewriting would discard real work and reset the bug surface. Aligns with Vrooli's 'edit existing files' guidance and lets this item finish in L effort instead of XL.

options.label: Greenfield rebuild — discard `scenarios/vrooli-events/ui/src/` and start over from the react-vite template
options.rationale: Clean slate, no inherited tech debt, but throws away ~1,949 LoC of working code and pushes effort well past L.

items.context: AnalyticsPage and ScenarioMetricsPage need chart visualizations (PRD REQ-UI-002 throughput chart, REQ-UI-003 per-scenario bar chart). No charting library is currently installed in `scenarios/vrooli-events/ui/package.json`. We need to pick one and install it.

options.label: Recharts
options.rationale: De facto standard across Vrooli scenarios — already used by agent-manager, deployment-manager, system-monitor, funnel-builder, scenario-auditor, social-media-scheduler, tech-tree-designer, ai-chatbot-manager. Tree-shakeable, declarative, plays well with React. Lowest cognitive load for any future contributor.

options.label: Visx (Airbnb)
options.rationale: Lower-level, more flexible, smaller runtime when used selectively, but no precedent in the codebase and steeper learning curve.

options.label: No charts — keep stat cards and tables only
options.rationale: Skips the chart requirement. Cheapest, but contradicts the backlog item description and PRD REQ-UI-002/003.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Provide your own chart library or approach

items.context: The current SettingsPage shows hard-coded values and explicitly says 'API-configurable retention is planned for a future release.' The description requires 'retention and storage settings management' (i.e., editable). This requires both a backend persistence + endpoint and a UI form.

options.label: Add backend `app_settings` table + GET/PUT `/api/v1/settings` + editable UI form; pruner reads live settings each cycle
options.rationale: Matches the description directly. Settings persist across restart, no env-var redeploys needed, validated server-side. Pruner reading the table once per 6h cycle is negligible overhead.

options.label: Keep SettingsPage read-only; expose env-var-driven config in docs and require restart to change
options.rationale: Lowest implementation cost, but contradicts 'settings management' in the description and forces operators to redeploy for routine ops changes.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Provide your own approach (e.g., file-based config, settings via CLI only)

items.context: A throughput chart needs time-bucketed event counts. We can either fetch raw events and aggregate in the browser, or add a backend rollup endpoint that returns pre-bucketed counts. Trade-off: client-side is simpler but pulls raw payloads; server-side is faster at scale but adds an endpoint.

options.label: Client-side aggregation: reuse `fetchEvents({limit: N})` and bucket by minute/hour in the chart component
options.rationale: No new endpoint; simpler. At current scale (single-node SQLite, sub-2GB store) the events query is fast and the browser handles bucketing trivially. Easiest to revert/iterate.

options.label: Backend rollup: add `GET /api/v1/events/stats?bucket=minute&since=...`
options.rationale: Pre-bucketed payload is small regardless of event volume; cleaner separation. Costs one new handler + tests + docs. Worth it if event volume might grow past tens of thousands per day.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Provide your own approach (e.g., dedicated rollups table maintained by the ingester)

items.context: Some pages have `.test.ts`, others (StreamPage, EventLogPage) don't. The existing `requirements-coverage.test.ts` only checks factory shapes, not rendered features. We need to decide how much testing to add as part of this item.

options.label: Vitest unit + component tests for new charts/forms + tests for previously-untested pages + light Playwright smoke for the dashboard golden path
options.rationale: Per Vrooli `feedback_testing_over_manual`, plans should use automated tests for verification. Component tests catch most regressions; one Playwright spec gives confidence that the running scenario actually serves the UI end-to-end. Modest extra effort.

options.label: Vitest unit + component tests only — no Playwright
options.rationale: Faster to write, no E2E infra to maintain, but no end-to-end confidence that the built UI talks to the running API correctly.

options.label: Add full Playwright E2E suite covering every page
options.rationale: Highest confidence, but significant additional effort and slower CI.

plan_updates: Created the initial scaffold of plan.md with all 14 mandatory sections. Captured: (1) the gap-fill nature of this item (existing scaffold is substantial), (2) the three core gaps (no charts, read-only settings, requirement-status drift), (3) a phased implementation strategy gated on the 5 pending workshop decisions, (4) contract decisions for the new /api/v1/settings endpoint and chart components, (5) testing plan covering both backend persistence and UI components, (6) risks including bundle-size, footgun retention values, and pre-existing failed policy-API item. Acceptance globs already cover ui/** and api/** — no spec update needed.
